question: Why isn't just treating sick patients enough to stop a waterborne disease outbreak?

options.A: The environmental reservoir remains contaminated and causes reinfection
options.B: Waterborne pathogens cannot be killed by boiling
options.C: Antibiotics do not work against bacteria found in water
options.D: Patients always become asymptomatic carriers after recovery

explanation: If you don't fix the dirty water supply, people will keep drinking it and falling right back sick. You've got to fix the source!

question: Which chemical messenger is mainly responsible for the brain's reward system and feelings of pleasure during drug use?

options.A: Hemoglobin
options.B: Dopamine
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: Nailed it! Dopamine is our feel-good chemical. Drugs flood the brain with it, creating an intense artificial high that tricks the reward system.

question: If you are calculating the incidence of a uterine infection, who belongs at the bottom (the denominator)?

options.A: Every single person living in the entire country
options.B: All children under the age of five years old
options.C: Only individuals with a uterus who are at risk
options.D: Only patients who already have the infection

explanation: Well done! The denominator should only include the people who are actually at risk of catching that specific condition.

question: Why is getting male partners involved in community safe motherhood programs so important in Nigeria?

options.A: They are solely responsible for performing postnatal physical examinations
options.B: They should be excluded from all prenatal health decisions
options.C: They act as primary birth attendants during complicated deliveries
options.D: They control household resources and support decisions to seek timely care

explanation: In many of our communities, men hold the purse strings and make transport decisions. Getting dads on board means transport and hospital fees get sorted faster!

question: Which of these is NOT a typical challenge when patients try to change their diet?

options.A: Unsupportive family members in the home
options.B: Financial constraints and high food costs
options.C: Excessive availability of free clinical dietitians
options.D: Lack of cooking skills or kitchen facilities

explanation: Correct! Having access to helpful dietitians is a blessing, not a barrier. The real struggles are usually money, time, and kitchen setups. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h6)

question: Where does Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) fit into the safety hierarchy for handling workplace hazards?

options.A: It is the last line of defense after other controls
options.B: It is only required after a toxic exposure has occurred
options.C: It replaces the need for proper chemical labelling
options.D: It is the primary method to eliminate workplace hazards

explanation: That's correct! PPE depends entirely on human behavior and proper wear, making it our last safety net if other controls fail. We always prefer removing the danger first.

question: A newly delivered mother needs support with lochia assessment and breastfeeding. Which midwife responsibility applies here?

options.A: Antenatal care
options.B: Postnatal care
options.C: Tertiary surgical care
options.D: Intrapartum care

explanation: Evaluating uterine involution, lochia, and helping with breastfeeding are all core components of postnatal care following delivery. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h2)

question: How do bones react when you do regular physical exercise and put mechanical stress on them?

options.A: They become fragile and brittle because osteoclasts destroy the matrix
options.B: They stop all cellular remodeling to conserve mineral reserves
options.C: They become thicker and stronger through increased osteoblast activity
options.D: They convert entirely from compact bone into spongy bone tissue

explanation: Use them and strengthen them! Exercise signals bone-building osteoblasts to lay down more material, making bones tough.

question: Why are taking baseline vital signs so important at the start of care?

options.A: To determine the patient's insurance coverage
options.B: To replace the need for taking a medical history
options.C: To compare against future readings to detect sudden changes
options.D: To calculate the exact date of patient discharge

explanation: Baselines give you a starting point. Later on, you can check new numbers against this baseline to spot if your patient is suddenly getting worse or improving.

question: What is the main goal of Primary Health Care (PHC) in a community?

options.A: Providing universally accessible and affordable essential health services
options.B: Focusing exclusively on surgical interventions for chronic illnesses
options.C: Building specialized tertiary hospitals in every local government area
options.D: Training only high-level medical consultants for village clinics

explanation: Think of PHC as bringing basic, affordable health care right to the doorsteps of the people who need it most. You've got this!

question: Which group of people needs extra protection and care in nursing research?

options.A: Staff registered nurses
options.B: Prisoners and children
options.C: Hospital chief executive officers
options.D: Experienced clinical instructors

explanation: Spot on! Children, prisoners, and unconscious patients need extra ethical safeguards because they might not be fully free to say yes or no. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h6)

question: Why should non-selective beta-blockers be used very carefully in patients with asthma?

options.A: They permanently destroy the tiny air sacs located at the base of the lungs
options.B: They cause the lungs to fill up with fluid within a few minutes of dosing
options.C: They stop asthma inhalers from working by coating the inside of the throat
options.D: They can block receptors in the lungs and trigger dangerous airway constriction

explanation: Non-selective beta-blockers affect receptors outside the heart, which can cause the smooth muscles in the airways to tighten. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h4)

question: A patient with breast cancer and bone metastases is drowsy, confused, and very weak. Which metabolic emergency is most likely occurring?

options.A: Hyponatremia
options.B: Tumor Lysis Syndrome
options.C: Hypercalcemia
options.D: Hypoglycemia

explanation: Tumors affecting the bones release excess calcium into the blood, causing neurological dullness, muscle weakness, and profound fatigue. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h2)

question: In research data, what is a 'wild code'?

options.A: A missing signature on a patient consent form
options.B: An emergency code called when a patient's heart stops
options.C: A secret password used to access the hospital computer network
options.D: A number that falls outside the allowed range of valid responses

explanation: A wild code is just an accidental typo—like typing '8' when a question only has options 1, 2, or 3!

question: How does nursing care in a half-way house differ from an acute hospital ward?

options.A: It focuses on rehabilitation, education, and community reintegration
options.B: It requires nurses to diagnose patients without a doctor present
options.C: It forbids nurses from talking to patients about their feelings
options.D: It relies entirely on physical restraints and locked isolation cells

explanation: Correct! Instead of dealing with emergency crises, residential nursing is all about teaching coping skills, guiding rehabilitation, and helping patients reconnect with society.

question: A patient admits to regularly eating undercooked pork. Which type of worm infection are they most at risk for?

options.A: Hookworm disease
options.B: Pinworm infestation
options.C: Tapeworm infection
options.D: Schistosomiasis

explanation: Undercooked pork is a well-known carrier for encysted pork tapeworm larvae. Cooking meat thoroughly is a simple way to protect patients!

question: You notice several patients in the surgical ward getting wound infections with similar signs. What should you do right away?

options.A: Report the cluster following hospital infection control protocols and review aseptic techniques.
options.B: Discharge all current patients immediately to close down the hospital wing.
options.C: Prescribe stronger antibiotics to all hospital staff members.
options.D: Wait until the end of the month to see if the infection rate drops naturally.

explanation: Catching an outbreak early is key! Always report the cluster to infection control and check your aseptic techniques to protect your patients.

question: What is the main downside of relying only on tertiary sources like textbooks for brand-new clinical questions?

options.A: They focus exclusively on qualitative patient interviews
options.B: They contain too much raw, unanalyzed patient data
options.C: They can lag behind the most recent primary research findings
options.D: They are always written by anonymous authors without credentials

explanation: Correct! Because textbooks take time to write and print, they might miss the absolute newest discoveries happening in the hospital wards right now.

question: Why is the nurse considered the central link in nutritional care for psychiatric patients?

options.A: They hold the legal authority to prescribe all specialized diets
options.B: They are the only team members trained in human biology
options.C: They dictate what medications the psychiatrist must order
options.D: They spend the most time with the patient and monitor daily habits

explanation: Correct! Because nurses are constantly around patients, they are in the best position to track real-time food intake and side effects.

question: How does healthy competition ideally affect providers in a free market?

options.A: It forces them to close their doors within a month
options.B: It encourages them to improve quality and manage costs
options.C: It eliminates the need for any nursing staff
options.D: It prevents them from purchasing new technology

explanation: Competition motivates businesses to attract consumers by offering better value, service quality, and efficiency. [learn more](GST322_U1_T4#GST322_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is it important for nurse managers to keep a close eye on ward inventory and supplies?

options.A: To ensure patients never pay for their medications
options.B: To calculate the daily income of every doctor
options.C: To prevent waste, expiration, and supply shortages
options.D: To increase the workload of junior nursing staff

explanation: Correct! Good inventory checks stop supplies from expiring on the shelf and ensure the ward never runs out during an emergency.

question: What is the golden rule of triage when responding to a major disaster?

options.A: Treating every single injured person in the exact order of arrival
options.B: Doing the greatest good for the greatest number of people
options.C: Sending all critical patients to the nearest small clinic
options.D: Focusing entirely on saving the person with the highest social status

explanation: In a disaster with scarce supplies, we shift our mindset from individual care to saving as many lives as our resources can possibly reach. Brilliant!

question: What is the main purpose of giving a patient a purgative?

options.A: To increase the absorption of water in the large intestine
options.B: To slow down gastrointestinal motility and prevent diarrhea
options.C: To promote bowel movements and relieve constipation
options.D: To neutralize excess stomach acid and soothe ulcers

explanation: You've got this! Purgatives are simply given to help clear the bowels and get things moving when a patient is constipated.

question: Who counts as a 'food handler' in a hospital or school setting?

options.A: Only the head chef in charge of the menu
options.B: The health inspector who visits monthly
options.C: Anyone who touches food, equipment, or utensils during prep or serving
options.D: Patients who eat the food provided

explanation: Anyone who comes into contact with food, plates, or cooking tools is considered a food handler. Safety starts with everyone!

question: How does unit dispensing help reduce financial waste in hospitals?

options.A: By tracking consumption accurately and allowing return of unsealed doses
options.B: By forcing patients to buy their medications from private vendors outside
options.C: By charging patients high penalty fees for missed medication doses
options.D: By eliminating the need for any professional pharmacy staff on duty

explanation: Precise tracking prevents excess purchasing, and sealed returned medications can be safely reissued to other patients. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is a likely consequence of poor communication among home health team members?

options.A: Conflicting instructions given to the patient and family
options.B: Reduced need for interprofessional documentation
options.C: Better alignment between nursing and therapy goals
options.D: Faster recovery times due to independent decision-making

explanation: When team members fail to communicate, patients and caregivers may receive mixed guidance, leading to confusion and safety risks. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h6)

question: In a healthy adult, about what percentage of total blood volume is made up of plasma?

options.A: Roughly 45 percent
options.B: Roughly 90 percent
options.C: Roughly 55 percent
options.D: Roughly 25 percent

explanation: Great job! Plasma makes up about 55% of your blood, while the remaining 45% is mostly red blood cells.

question: Why might two people taking the exact same dose of cough syrup react completely differently?

options.A: The color of the syrup changes how fast the stomach digests it.
options.B: Different brands use completely different active ingredients.
options.C: The time of day changes the weight of the medication.
options.D: Genetic differences in liver enzymes affect drug breakdown rates.

explanation: We all process drugs at our own pace because of our unique liver enzymes (like CYP2D6)! One person might clear it fast, while another feels it much longer.

question: What is the main purpose of establishing a clear case definition in surveillance?

options.A: Determining the exact cost of hospital treatment for insurance claims
options.B: Speeding up the time it takes to prescribe antibiotics to a patient
options.C: Fulfilling administrative paperwork requirements without clinical value
options.D: Ensuring everyone uses the exact same criteria to identify a disease

explanation: A standard case definition ensures that health workers across different regions are counting the exact same illness criteria. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why is the rectal route frequently used for pediatric fever management?

options.A: It avoids the struggle of forcing bitter syrups down a sick child's throat
options.B: Children absorb all medications ten times faster rectally than orally
options.C: Suppositories never melt prematurely in young children
options.D: It eliminates the need for any hand hygiene during administration

explanation: Infants and young children often spit out oral medications, so antipyretic suppositories provide a reliable alternative. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h5)

question: How can nurses help stop community members from hiding infectious illnesses out of fear?

options.A: Refusing to treat patients who do not speak English
options.B: Keeping all health information secret from local leaders
options.C: Threatening penalties for families that miss immunization days
options.D: Building trust through health education and supportive care

explanation: When we show empathy, educate gently, and create a safe space without judgment, community members feel comfortable coming to us early.

question: What is one of the biggest challenges when grading students during clinical postings?

options.A: Not having enough patients in the hospital
options.B: Instructor bias and subjective grading
options.C: Having too many multiple-choice questions
options.D: Using too many computer programs

explanation: Since humans do the watching in the wards, different clinical tutors might score the exact same student performance differently. It can be tricky!

question: You notice the safety box on your treatment trolley is about three-quarters full. What should you do?

options.A: Seal the container and replace it with a new one
options.B: Push the contents down firmly with a gloved hand to create more space
options.C: Transfer some needles into a regular black plastic bag
options.D: Leave it open until the end of the week to save money

explanation: Safety first! Never push down or overfill sharp containers. Seal them at three-quarters full to prevent accidental needle pricks.

question: What does incidence measure in a population?

options.A: The number of new cases diagnosed
options.B: The total number of existing cases
options.C: The percentage of people who die
options.D: The cost of treating the disease

explanation: Incidence specifically counts the new diagnoses appearing over a set timeframe, showing the rate at which a disease develops. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h3)

question: If your research question asks if handwashing education decreases hospital infections, how should your hypothesis look?

options.A: Units with handwashing education will have lower infection rates
options.B: What is the average rate of hospital-acquired infections?
options.C: Handwashing education has no impact on hospital infections
options.D: Does handwashing education decrease hospital infection rates?

explanation: You take your research question and turn it into a confident, testable prediction statement!

question: What makes ethical choices so emotionally heavy for nurses during a major disaster?

options.A: Having to ration scarce life-saving resources among many needy patients
options.B: Having too many modern medical machines to choose from
options.C: Working in fully air-conditioned and quiet field offices
options.D: Patients having unlimited time to discuss treatment options

explanation: So true. Deciding who gets scarce life-saving care when there isn't enough to go around is one of the hardest emotional burdens a nurse can carry.

question: In nursing research, what do we mean by the word 'population'?

options.A: Every person living in the city where the study takes place
options.B: The specific patients who dropped out of a clinical trial
options.C: The entire group of people the researcher wants to study
options.D: Only the nurses working in a specific hospital ward

explanation: You've got this! In research, the 'population' is just the big group of people you are curious about and want to learn more from. Think of it as the big picture before you zoom in.

question: What is a major benefit of a man attending antenatal care visits with his partner?

options.A: He replaces the midwife during delivery
options.B: He can perform the physical examination himself
options.C: He learns about pregnancy danger signs and birth preparedness
options.D: He receives free medications for chronic illnesses

explanation: Attending antenatal visits helps fathers understand what complications to watch out for and how to prepare for emergencies. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h3)

question: What is the primary long-term clinical use for thiazide diuretics?

options.A: Reducing intracranial pressure
options.B: Treating severe pulmonary edema
options.C: Treating chronic hypertension
options.D: Reversing acute kidney failure

explanation: Thiazides provide a steady, mild diuretic and blood vessel relaxing effect, making them standard first-line therapy for high blood pressure. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h4)

question: Why does eating a high-protein diet often help people naturally eat fewer calories overall?

options.A: It increases feelings of fullness and satiety
options.B: It completely blocks the absorption of dietary fats
options.C: It lowers the body temperature during digestion
options.D: It speeds up the removal of water weight

explanation: Protein takes longer to digest and sends fullness signals to your brain. This naturally keeps hunger at bay so you don't feel the need to overeat!

question: Why are benzodiazepines generally prescribed for short-term use only during sudden, severe anxiety?

options.A: They permanently cure the underlying brain chemistry imbalance in one dose
options.B: They stop working entirely after the very first day of administration
options.C: They carry a significant risk of tolerance and physical dependence
options.D: They immediately cause severe permanent organ damage if used at all

explanation: Spot on! The body gets used to benzodiazepines very quickly, which can lead to dependence and addiction if taken for too long.

question: Why are sharps containers made with hard, thick plastic walls?

options.A: To allow the containers to be reused multiple times safely
options.B: To dissolve the metal needles chemically inside the box
options.C: To make the bins heavy enough to stay upright on carts
options.D: To prevent needles from piercing through and injuring handlers

explanation: Spot on! Those tough walls ensure used needles won't accidentally poke right through and stick anyone handling the box.

question: Why must a nurse researcher be extra careful when asking their own hospital patients to join a study?

options.A: Patients always know more about research than the nurses do
options.B: Patients might feel pressured to agree out of fear of poor care
options.C: Patients are legally barred from signing consent forms
options.D: Hospital management forbids nurses from talking to patients

explanation: Spot on! Patients might feel too scared to say 'no' because they worry it might affect the medical care they get from the ward. We must always make participation 100% voluntary!

question: Which type of sensory receptors inside the ear pick up sound and movement?

options.A: Chemoreceptors
options.B: Photoreceptors
options.C: Thermoreceptors
options.D: Mechanoreceptors

explanation: Think 'mechanical'! Mechanoreceptors respond to physical forces like sound waves and fluid movement in the ear.

question: When designing a daily meal, which part should you usually plan first?

options.A: Main dishes like proteins and primary starches
options.B: Desserts and sugary snacks
options.C: Garnishes and table napkins
options.D: Beverages and drinking water

explanation: The proteins and starches are the heavy lifters of the meal; you build the rest around them!

question: How does the delayed maturation of the prefrontal cortex affect teenage decision-making regarding sex?

options.A: It makes it harder for teens to pause and think through the long-term risks of their actions
options.B: It prevents teenagers from feeling any physical attraction to others
options.C: It causes complete memory loss of safe sex education
options.D: It eliminates all emotional responses to relationships

explanation: Because the prefrontal cortex is still developing, teenagers struggle with impulse control and evaluating future dangers, making impulsive sexual choices more likely. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h2)

question: Why do midwives and doctors check red blood cell indices (like MCV) in an anemic pregnant woman?

options.A: To determine the specific structural classification and underlying cause of the anaemia
options.B: To check if the mother has developed gestational diabetes
options.C: To measure the exact volume of amniotic fluid surrounding the fetus
options.D: To calculate the precise delivery date based on red cell lifespan

explanation: Brilliant! MCV tells you the size of the red blood cells. Are they too small (microcytic), too big (macrocytic), or normal? That helps you know if it's iron trouble, folate trouble, or something else.

question: A nurse notices patient call bells take much longer to answer during evening shifts. What is the best systems-thinking response?

options.A: Map out evening workloads, staffing numbers, and task layouts to find the bottleneck
options.B: Tell the evening nurses they are lazy and need to walk faster
options.C: Ignore it because evening shifts are always chaotic
options.D: Punish the nurse sitting closest to the front desk

explanation: Looking for structural bottlenecks instead of throwing blame is the core of systems thinking in nursing leadership.

question: Why must blood-soaked dressings be treated as hazardous infectious waste?

options.A: They contain live germs that can spread disease
options.B: They are made of synthetic plastic fibers
options.C: They take too long to decompose naturally
options.D: They are heavy and expensive to transport

explanation: Items soaked in body fluids carry active pathogens that can easily infect anyone handling them without care. Safety first! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h3)

question: Why is Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) described as an ongoing cycle rather than a single event?

options.A: Because medical equipment never breaks down more than once
options.B: Because hospital management loves writing endless reports every week
options.C: Because healthcare delivery and patient needs are always changing
options.D: Because nurses have too much free time during their shifts

explanation: CQI is continuous because healthcare environments are dynamic, requiring constant monitoring and small adjustments to maintain high standards. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h6)

question: What is the main difference between an acute care EHR and an ambulatory EHR?

options.A: Acute care systems focus on round-the-clock hospital monitoring, while ambulatory systems track long-term outpatient visits
options.B: Acute care systems prohibit nurses from charting, whereas ambulatory systems are strictly for nursing documentation
options.C: Ambulatory systems can only be accessed inside intensive care units using desktop computers
options.D: Ambulatory systems require minute-by-minute surgical checklists, while acute care systems only track yearly checkups

explanation: Spot on! Acute care is for the hustle and bustle of 24/7 hospital wards, while ambulatory care tracks regular visits at out-patient clinics.

question: Which common virus is strongly linked to the development of cervical cancer?

options.A: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.B: Human Papillomavirus
options.C: Epstein-Barr virus
options.D: Hepatitis B virus

explanation: High-risk strains of HPV can cause changes in cervical cells over time. This is why screening and the HPV vaccine are such big wins in public health!

question: How does a Clinical Decision Support (CDS) feature protect hospitalized patients?

options.A: By printing out paper charts for family members to review at home
options.B: By automatically ordering emergency laboratory tests without doctor approval
options.C: By locking the computer screen whenever a nurse leaves the patient bedside
options.D: By popping up automated warnings about drug allergies or unsafe medication dosages

explanation: CDS tools act as safety nets by analyzing patient data in real time and alerting staff to potential clinical risks before harm occurs. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h3)

question: A hospital encourages nurses to log medication errors openly so the team can review them. Which core component does this action demonstrate?

options.A: Financial culture
options.B: Executive culture
options.C: Reporting culture
options.D: Punitive culture

explanation: A reporting culture exists when workers feel safe enough to document and share information about errors and near-misses. [learn more](GST319_U6_T6#GST319_U6_T6_h2)

question: What happens right away during the emission phase?

options.A: Urine is forced out of the kidneys
options.B: Semen gathers in the prostatic urethra
options.C: The external sphincter permanently relaxes
options.D: Sperm are newly created in the bladder

explanation: Emission is just the gathering step—sperm and fluids team up and wait in the upper urethra before the big push outward!

question: When you hear 'quantitative research', what kind of data immediately comes to mind?

options.A: Unstructured audio recordings of interviews
options.B: Numerical data and measurable variables
options.C: Handwritten patient diary entries
options.D: Detailed personal stories and life histories

explanation: Think 'Q for Quantity'! Quantitative research is all about numbers, measurements, and stats to find answers.

question: A pot of cooked rice was left on the table for 5 hours on a warm afternoon. What should be done with it?

options.A: Place the rice straight into the freezer for future meals.
options.B: Reheat the rice thoroughly on the stove to kill all toxins.
options.C: Wash the rice with clean water before serving it again.
options.D: Discard the rice because it sat too long in the Danger Zone.

explanation: Leaving food out too long lets germs multiply and make toxins that heat cannot fix. When in doubt, throw it out to keep patients safe!

question: What two things does a Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY) combine?

options.A: Both the quantity and the quality of life lived
options.B: Direct medical costs and indirect wage losses
options.C: Nurse staffing ratios and patient satisfaction ratings
options.D: Hospital operational costs and patient travel expenses

explanation: QALY looks at the bigger picture: it measures not just how long a patient lives, but how good and pain-free those years are.

question: A client wants a method she can insert herself vaginally hours before intercourse to block sperm. Which supply method is this?

options.A: Diaphragm with spermicide
options.B: Emergency hormonal pill
options.C: Combined oral contraceptive pill
options.D: Male latex condom

explanation: A diaphragm is a dome-shaped barrier a woman places inside to cover her cervix, especially when paired with sperm-killing cream. Spot on!

question: What is raw, unorganized clinical measurements like a single heart rate reading considered?

options.A: Information
options.B: Knowledge
options.C: Wisdom
options.D: Data

explanation: Raw facts and numbers without context are classified as data before they are analyzed or interpreted. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T7#GNS113_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which clinical sign points more toward a clotting factor problem like haemophilia rather than a platelet issue?

options.A: Petechiae scattered across the lower legs
options.B: Frequent, mild nosebleeds that stop within minutes
options.C: Tiny red spots on the skin after minor pressure
options.D: Bleeding into large joints like the knees and elbows

explanation: Bleeding into big joints (called hemarthrosis) is a classic trademark of factor deficiencies like haemophilia. Petechiae and nosebleeds are usually more about platelet trouble.

question: A nurse is feeling very anxious after a traumatic patient incident on the ward. Where should they turn for immediate, supportive help from fellow health workers?

options.A: The public relations department for media statements
options.B: The legal department for liability review
options.C: A hospital-sponsored peer support team
options.D: The billing office for patient records

explanation: Peer support teams are specially trained to offer a comforting shoulder and an empathetic ear when ward incidents shake your confidence.

question: What is an example of a 'forcing function' used to keep patients safe in a hospital?

options.A: Verbally reminding nurses to check blood pressure twice a shift
options.B: Hanging warning signs near every medication storage cabinet
options.C: Punishing staff members who forget to sign documentation sheets
options.D: Feeding tubes that physically cannot connect to intravenous lines

explanation: A forcing function is brilliant because it uses physical design to make a dangerous mistake literally impossible—like making ports that only fit the correct tubing!

question: What protective layers wrap around both the brain and the spinal cord?

options.A: Meninges
options.B: Ventricles
options.C: Myelin sheaths
options.D: Synapses

explanation: The meninges are like sturdy cushion layers wrapped around your delicate central nervous system for safety. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h3)

question: What does the abbreviation 'bid' mean on a medication order?

options.A: As needed
options.B: Before meals
options.C: Twice a day
options.D: Three times a day

explanation: You've got this! 'Bid' comes from the Latin 'bis in die', which simply means twice daily. You'll see this all the time on drug charts!

question: Why is it so important to keep interruptions in chest compressions to a bare minimum when using an AED?

options.A: The AED machine will shut down if compressions continue too long
options.B: Stopping compressions lowers blood flow to the brain and heart
options.C: Pausing compressions causes the AED pads to lose their sticky adhesive
options.D: Continuous motion prevents the AED from detecting breathing sounds

explanation: Every second you pause compressions, blood pressure drops and the brain loses vital oxygen. Keep your hands on the chest as much as possible!

question: Why is it a good idea to soak a patient's nails in warm water before trimming them?

options.A: It softens the hard nail plate and cuticles for easier trimming
options.B: It permanently kills all bacteria hiding under the nail bed
options.C: It stops the patient from feeling any cold drafts in the room
options.D: It opens up the pores so the skin absorbs extra vitamins

explanation: Spot on! Warm water softens up the hard keratin, making clipping smooth and saving your patient from painful splits or cracks.

question: What is an important duty for a community health nurse visiting a family with a physically disabled member?

options.A: Providing legal representation in court for disability benefits
options.B: Managing the financial accounts of local community health clinics
options.C: Performing complex orthopedic surgeries within the home environment
options.D: Conducting household assessments and teaching proper transfer techniques

explanation: Home safety checks and teaching family members safe transfer moves keep both the patient and the caregiver safe from injury. Wonderful practice!

question: When were the very first official Recommended Dietary Allowances introduced?

options.A: During the chemical revolution of Lavoisier
options.B: During the discovery of vitamin C
options.C: During the ancient Roman Empire
options.D: During World War II

explanation: Correct! Governments needed a way to ensure soldiers and citizens stayed healthy despite wartime food rationing, so they set these standard allowances.

question: What do home ovulation predictor kits mainly test for in urine?

options.A: Human chorionic gonadotropin
options.B: Luteinizing hormone
options.C: Basal body temperature
options.D: Estrogen metabolites only

explanation: Ovulation kits look for that telltale surge of luteinizing hormone in the urine, which usually happens a day or two before ovulation.

question: What is the main goal of nursing care when we want to help a patient improve their adaptation skills?

options.A: To ensure the patient relies permanently on hospital staff
options.B: To eliminate all stress from the patient's external environment
options.C: To replace maladaptive habits with healthy coping skills
options.D: To force the patient to forget all past traumatic events

explanation: We can't wrap our patients in cotton wool or remove all stress. Our goal is to coach them toward flexible, healthy ways to weather life's storms!

question: A patient facing severe financial hardship asks you about family planning. What is her money constraint most likely to affect?

options.A: Her natural immunity against common infections
options.B: Her ability to consistently buy and use modern contraceptives
options.C: Her biological response to hormonal medications
options.D: Her genetic predisposition to chronic illnesses

explanation: That's right! Money worries directly affect purchasing power, making it tough to afford steady supplies of birth control.

question: What is the main medical benefit of Female Genital Mutilation (FGM)?

options.A: It improves long-term reproductive health
options.B: It balances female reproductive hormones
options.C: It has no medical purpose or health benefits
options.D: It prevents common bacterial infections

explanation: You got this! FGM is done strictly for cultural or traditional reasons. It doesn't offer any health benefits to the body at all.

question: Which two nutrients are most important for keeping older adults' bones strong?

options.A: Vitamin C and iron
options.B: Sodium and potassium
options.C: Calcium and vitamin D
options.D: Vitamin A and zinc

explanation: Calcium is the building block for bones, and vitamin D is the helper vitamin that lets the gut absorb that calcium!

question: How do non-sterile gloves affect your hand hygiene routine during medication rounds?

options.A: Gloves make skin completely impervious to all bacterial transfer
options.B: Hand rubs should only be applied directly over dirty gloves
options.C: Gloves do not replace the need for proper hand hygiene
options.D: Wearing gloves eliminates the requirement for washing hands

explanation: Gloves can have tiny invisible tears, and your hands can easily pick up germs while taking them off. Always wash your hands before and after wearing gloves!

question: A panel of senior nurses reviews a new questionnaire to see if it covers every aspect of post-operative care. What are they testing?

options.A: Content validity
options.B: Physical durability
options.C: Data entry speed
options.D: Test-retest reliability

explanation: Content validity ensures that the tool covers all important dimensions of the subject being studied. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h6)

question: What is the key difference between summarizing and synthesizing literature?

options.A: Grouping multiple studies together by themes and trends
options.B: Deleting any study that disagrees with your personal opinion
options.C: Copying abstracts word-for-word into your own paper
options.D: Listing every single article in strict chronological order

explanation: Synthesis means weaving different studies together around common themes, rather than just listing one summary after another.

question: What is the main goal of palliative care?

options.A: To speed up the dying process
options.B: To cure the underlying disease
options.C: To provide long-term rehabilitation therapy
options.D: To improve quality of life for patients and families

explanation: You've got this! Palliative care is all about bringing comfort, easing pain, and making life as good as possible for patients and their loved ones, rather than trying to cure the illness.

question: Why must reusable equipment like stethoscopes be wiped with disinfectant between patients?

options.A: To prevent cross-contamination and hospital-acquired infections
options.B: To keep the metal parts from rusting in humid weather
options.C: To remove any manufacturer dust from the surface
options.D: To ensure the sound quality remains clear for hearing

explanation: Medical tools can easily carry germs from one patient to another if they are not cleaned properly. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h3)

question: Which PHC principle ensures that rural and underserved populations get a fair share of health services?

options.A: Tertiary specialization
options.B: Technological centralization
options.C: Equitable distribution
options.D: Commercial privatization

explanation: Equitable distribution simply means fairness—making sure health resources reach everyone, especially vulnerable groups who need them most.

question: How do modern apology laws treat expressions of sympathy from healthcare providers?

options.A: They remove all licensing requirements for doctors involved in adverse events
options.B: They force the hospital to pay double compensation in every civil lawsuit
options.C: They protect humanitarian expressions of sorrow from being used as evidence of fault
options.D: They make it illegal for any nurse to speak directly to a patient's family

explanation: Apology protection laws encourage honesty by making sure that showing human empathy and sorrow cannot be used in court as proof of guilt.

question: What is the normal resting breathing rate for a healthy adult?

options.A: 30 to 40 breaths per minute
options.B: 8 to 12 breaths per minute
options.C: 20 to 30 breaths per minute
options.D: 12 to 20 breaths per minute

explanation: Healthy adults take between 12 and 20 breaths every minute while resting. Easy to remember for your exams! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h4)

question: What does providing integrated services mean in an adolescent clinic?

options.A: Requiring both parents to attend every medical consultation with the teen
options.B: Using traditional medicine alongside modern pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: Offering multiple health services like reproductive and mental care under one roof
options.D: Combining adult and adolescent patients in the same waiting room

explanation: Integrated services mean a young person can access different types of healthcare in a single convenient location. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h5)

question: Losing how much weight unintentionally in a single month is a major red flag for malnutrition?

options.A: Any weight loss at all
options.B: More than five percent
options.C: Ten pounds regardless of body size
options.D: Exactly one percent

explanation: Great job! Dropping over 5% of your body weight in a month is a serious warning sign that needs quick attention.

question: You notice false health rumors spreading rapidly during a disease outbreak. What is the best action to take?

options.A: Ignore the rumors because they will eventually fade away
options.B: Report the community members spreading rumors to the police
options.C: Actively communicate correct safety updates and debunk the rumors
options.D: Wait for international health organizations to issue a formal ban

explanation: Well done! Addressing misinformation directly prevents panic and keeps people focused on accurate health actions.

question: How should a nurse instruct a patient to use nystatin oral suspension for mouth thrush?

options.A: Swallow the liquid immediately on an empty stomach with a full glass of water
options.B: Swish the liquid thoroughly around the mouth before swallowing it
options.C: Dilute the entire bottle in a glass of cold fruit juice and drink it fast
options.D: Gargle the liquid at the back of the throat and spit it out without swallowing

explanation: Correct! The medication needs time to touch all the infected spots in the mouth before it is swallowed down to coat the throat or gut.

question: Why must diet care in Nigeria make use of local staples like garri, beans, and yams?

options.A: Because local staples contain zero carbohydrates and cannot raise blood sugar
options.B: To make sure the meal advice is affordable, practical, and fits the patient's culture
options.C: Because imported foreign foods are illegal to prescribe in government hospitals
options.D: To prevent the Ministry of Health from auditing the hospital kitchen

explanation: Patients find it much easier to stick to meal plans when they use foods they already know, buy, and love eating every day.

question: Which organ in the body is the main factory for producing most of our blood clotting factors?

options.A: Spleen
options.B: Liver
options.C: Kidney
options.D: Pancreas

explanation: The liver is a busy chemical plant! It produces almost all the important proteins needed for blood to clot properly.

question: Why must pregnant women attend antenatal clinics even when they feel completely fine?

options.A: Pregnant women are legally required to visit the clinic every single week
options.B: It is impossible to eat a balanced diet without clinic supervision
options.C: Clinics require attendance records to secure international funding
options.D: Dangerous conditions like high blood pressure can develop without early warning signs

explanation: Exactly! Silent issues like pre-eclampsia or anemia can build up inside without any obvious signs at first. Routine checks keep both mum and baby safe.

question: A baby with severe diarrhea is too weak to drink and shows signs of severe dehydration. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Administer high-dose antidiarrheal syrup
options.B: Start emergency intravenous fluid resuscitation
options.C: Wait for laboratory stool culture results
options.D: Send the child home with oral rehydration packets

explanation: When a child is too weak to drink and dangerously dehydrated, rush IV fluids are needed immediately to save their life. You are learning critical emergency steps!

question: What is the coolest superpower of adaptive immunity compared to innate immunity?

options.A: It relies entirely on physical skin barriers to keep germs out
options.B: It creates immunological memory for faster responses to repeat infections
options.C: It provides instant protection within minutes of touching a pathogen
options.D: It does not require white blood cells to eliminate foreign microbes

explanation: Adaptive immunity never forgets a face! It remembers specific germs it has fought before, so if the same germ shows up again, it attacks much faster and stronger.

question: What is a major contributing factor to caregiver burden in palliative home care?

options.A: Excessive amounts of free time available to family members
options.B: Juggling household duties, financial stress, and nursing care
options.C: Having too many professional nurses visiting the home
options.D: The patient refusing to eat hospital-prepared meals

explanation: Family caregivers often shoulder overwhelming multi-role responsibilities without adequate rest, leading to burnout. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h4)

question: What is the main difference in how drug treatment is chosen for type 1 versus type 2 diabetes?

options.A: Type 1 is managed strictly through lifestyle changes without drugs
options.B: Type 2 patients never need insulin under any clinical circumstances
options.C: Type 2 can only be treated with injectable non-insulin medications
options.D: Type 1 always requires insulin, while type 2 often starts with oral agents

explanation: Well done! Because type 1 diabetes means the body doesn't make insulin at all, replacement therapy is needed right from the start.

question: What is the main benefit of regular disaster drills in a community?

options.A: It completely stops natural disasters from happening
options.B: It reduces panic and builds muscle memory for safe evacuation
options.C: It guarantees that no property damage will ever occur
options.D: It replaces the need for building structural flood walls

explanation: Well done! Practice makes calm; drills help people respond automatically and safely during real emergencies.

question: What is the typical timeframe covered by a tactical plan?

options.A: One to three years
options.B: One to seven days
options.C: A few hours
options.D: Ten to twenty years

explanation: Tactical plans are medium-term guides that usually span a period of one to three years. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h3)

question: How do mass movements differ from regular mixing movements in the large intestine?

options.A: Segmental movements require conscious effort to move waste.
options.B: Segmental contractions happen only once or twice a day.
options.C: Mass movements push stool a long way toward the rectum all at once.
options.D: Mass movements happen non-stop all day and night.

explanation: Mass movements are like big, powerful waves that sweep through the colon every now and then to clear out stored waste toward the exit. You've got this!

question: Which lifestyle advice is most important for a nurse to emphasize during patient education for sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Restrict fluid intake in the evening to prevent frequent nighttime urination
options.B: Maintain consistent daily hydration and avoid extreme temperature changes
options.C: Wear tight, supportive clothing to keep the peripheral blood vessels compressed
options.D: Engage in intense competitive sports to build strong cardiovascular endurance

explanation: Drinking plenty of water prevents the blood from thickening, and avoiding cold temperatures stops blood vessels from narrowing, both of which prevent crises. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h7)

question: What is the very first link in the chain of infection?

options.A: Susceptible host
options.B: Portal of entry
options.C: Mode of transmission
options.D: Causative agent

explanation: Think of the causative agent as the starting point—it's the actual germ (like bacteria or a virus) that causes the disease!

question: Why is it best practice for nurses to involve community leaders when planning health programs?

options.A: It prevents NGOs from ever visiting rural communities
options.B: It fosters local ownership and reduces cultural resistance to care
options.C: It removes the need for nurses to document patient treatments
options.D: It ensures that healthcare providers receive financial bonuses

explanation: When local leaders are part of the plan, the community feels respected, trusts the process, and joins in willingly.

question: Why are structured templates and drop-down menus in electronic charts so helpful for student and staff nurses?

options.A: By prompting clinicians to record all required assessment elements
options.B: By automatically discharging patients when vitals stabilize
options.C: By locking nurses out of charts until their shift officially ends
options.D: By removing the legal requirement to sign nursing notes

explanation: You got it! Templates act as a gentle guide so you don't accidentally forget to document vital assessment details. It keeps everyone's charting thorough and consistent.

question: What is the purpose of using the 'teach-back' method during patient education?

options.A: Asking the patient to repeat instructions in their own words
options.B: Testing the patient on medical history terminology
options.C: Reading a medical textbook aloud to the family
options.D: Having the nurse lecture for an hour without stopping

explanation: Teach-back is brilliant: you ask them to explain your instructions back to you in their own words so you know they truly understand.

question: A patient with a healing skin rash is stepped down to a milder lotion. What is the goal of this change?

options.A: To remove the need for any further skin assessments
options.B: To completely stop all moisture from reaching the skin
options.C: To maintain skin healing without causing local side effects
options.D: To increase the absorption speed of the original drug

explanation: We use weaker strengths as healing progresses to protect the skin safely without over-treating it. Great job keeping the patient's comfort in mind!

question: How does a receptor antagonist antidote work to reverse an overdose?

options.A: It binds to heavy metals and flushes them out through the urine
options.B: It attaches to the same cell sites as the poison to block its action
options.C: It coats the lining of the stomach so the poison cannot pass through
options.D: It destroys the chemical structure of the poison inside the blood

explanation: Think of it like musical chairs! The antagonist rushes in and sits on the cell receptors first, blocking the poison from grabbing a seat and doing damage.

question: What is the main limitation of using a 24-hour dietary recall?

options.A: It relies heavily on the patient's memory and may not show normal eating habits
options.B: It is too expensive for routine use in busy outpatient clinics
options.C: It requires the patient to write down every meal for an entire month
options.D: It only measures fluid intake and ignores solid foods entirely

explanation: A single day may represent an unusual eating day, such as a holiday or a day of illness, and patients often forget items they consumed. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h4)

question: What immediate action should a nurse take if a quarantined person develops a sudden fever?

options.A: Reclassify the person as a suspected case and arrange for testing
options.B: Discharge the person immediately to clear space in the facility
options.C: Administer strong antibiotics without informing the doctor
options.D: Tell the person to ignore it until the quarantine period ends

explanation: Developing symptoms means the person may now be infected and requires prompt isolation and diagnostic evaluation. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why should approved drug prices be clearly posted on notice boards near hospital pharmacies?

options.A: To advertise the hospital services to private pharmaceutical competitors
options.B: To comply with international tax collection laws
options.C: To encourage patients to donate money to the pharmacy
options.D: To ensure transparency and prevent staff from overcharging patients

explanation: Transparency is key! Displaying official prices openly protects vulnerable patients from exploitation and keeps everyone honest.

question: What is the first and most effective step to control severe external bleeding from a limb wound?

options.A: Elevating the injured arm or leg above the heart
options.B: Giving the patient oral fluids immediately
options.C: Applying direct firm pressure to the wound
options.D: Washing the wound thoroughly with cold water

explanation: Direct pressure helps compress the damaged blood vessels and allows a blood clot to form over the injury site. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h5)

question: What does a route of transmission describe?

options.A: The path a germ takes from a source to a new host
options.B: The specific medication used to kill a virus
options.C: The time it takes for symptoms to show up
options.D: The physical strength of a bacterial cell wall

explanation: The route of transmission is simply the way an infectious agent moves from its reservoir to reach a susceptible person. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which piece of advice should a nurse give a patient to prevent food and drug mix-ups?

options.A: Take all medications with grapefruit juice to help speed up absorption in the stomach
options.B: Check with your healthcare provider before starting any new herbal or over-the-counter products
options.C: Crush all of your tablets together in the morning to make them easier to swallow with juice
options.D: Stop taking your prescribed medications whenever you feel completely back to normal

explanation: Always remind patients to ask an expert before mixing everyday supplements, herbs, or shop-bought meds with their hospital prescriptions. Safety first!

question: What is the very first step a nurse must take to become truly culturally competent?

options.A: Insist that patients adopt modern hospital habits
options.B: Abandon all western medical training completely
options.C: Examine their own personal biases and values
options.D: Memorize the medical laws of every country

explanation: Self-reflection is key! Before we can understand others, we have to look inward and recognize our own unique cultural viewpoints and biases.

question: During a home visit, a nurse notices a psychiatric client is also suffering from severe untreated malnutrition and extreme poverty. What is the best next step?

options.A: Discharge the client from psychiatric care permanently
options.B: Tell the family to borrow money immediately from a bank
options.C: Refer the client to social welfare and appropriate support agencies
options.D: Ignore the poverty because nurses only treat mental symptoms

explanation: Holistic community care requires linking clients with social welfare services when poverty and malnutrition impact their health. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h7)

question: What is the main job of a septic tank in an individual home's waste system?

options.A: To allow solids to settle and liquids to flow out to a drain field
options.B: To store rainwater for washing clothes and watering gardens
options.C: To incinerate solid waste using high-voltage electric heating
options.D: To pump treated drinking water directly back into household taps

explanation: Think of a septic tank as a settling room: heavy solids sink to the bottom, while the liquid wastewater flows out gently into the underground drain field for natural filtering.

question: Why are DRF drug prices kept lower than regular commercial pharmacies?

options.A: To ensure low-income patients can afford essential treatments
options.B: To punish private pharmacy owners for overcharging people
options.C: To make patients buy more drugs than they actually need
options.D: To drive private pharmaceutical companies completely out of business

explanation: Exactly! Public hospitals use DRFs to protect everyday people from suffering or extreme poverty just because they need basic medicine.

question: Why is it so helpful for nurses to involve family caregivers in the care plan for an autistic patient?

options.A: Caregivers know the patient's unique routines and communication cues best
options.B: Caregivers have formal medical degrees in nursing care
options.C: Hospital policy legally requires family members to do the nursing work
options.D: It removes all responsibility from the hospital staff

explanation: Family members are absolute experts on their loved one's specific triggers and favorite comforts. Partnering with them makes all the difference!

question: A newborn baby experiences cold stress, leading to low oxygen levels in the blood. What is most likely to happen to their lung blood vessels?

options.A: They will dilate and drop lung resistance further
options.B: They will convert directly into permanent ligaments
options.C: They will constrict and keep lung resistance high
options.D: They will force the ductus venosus to stay open

question: What kind of healthcare workers typically deliver care at Tier 3 of the pyramid?

options.A: Non-specialized health workers like general nurses and primary health staff
options.B: Humanitarian logistics officers
options.C: Specialized psychiatrists and neuroscientists only
options.D: Only traditional spiritual healers

explanation: Exactly! Tier 3 is where general nurses and clinic staff step in to provide focused, non-specialized support like counseling.

question: What is the best first step when looking at a research table for the first time?

options.A: Jump straight to the bottom right corner for the final total
options.B: Assume the data is correct without checking the labels
options.C: Read the title and row labels to understand the context
options.D: Look for spelling mistakes in the column headers

explanation: Always check the title and labels first! It gives you the big picture so the numbers start making sense right away.

question: How must controlled medications like morphine be kept safe on a hospital ward?

options.A: Unlocked inside the general treatment room
options.B: In an open plastic tray on the main desk
options.C: Inside the patient's bedside drawer for privacy
options.D: Inside a double-locked secure cupboard

explanation: Correct! Controlled drugs are powerful and prone to abuse, so they always live in a secure double-locked space.

question: What is a major health risk for homebound clients who experience long-term loneliness and social isolation?

options.A: Rapid increase in bone mineral density
options.B: Improved short-term memory function
options.C: Enhanced cardiovascular endurance
options.D: Weakened immune responses and cognitive decline

explanation: Humans are social creatures! Lack of interaction takes a heavy toll on both body and mind, making it easier to fall sick and harder to stay sharp.

question: A pregnant woman misses her antenatal visits because she cannot afford transport or clinic fees. Which factor is mainly affecting her health?

options.A: Political party affiliation
options.B: Socio-economic factors
options.C: Cultural taboos
options.D: Genetic factors

explanation: Spot on! Financial struggles and poverty are classic examples of socio-economic factors that make it hard for patients to access care. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core characteristic of a good healthcare plan?

options.A: Simplicity
options.B: Flexibility
options.C: Feasibility
options.D: Rigidity

explanation: Good plans must bend and adapt, so rigidity makes a plan fail when unexpected clinical situations arise. [learn more](GST321_U1_T7#GST321_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why is having family support especially helpful for patients managing HIV?

options.A: It lowers depression and improves treatment retention
options.B: It eliminates the need for routine laboratory testing
options.C: It removes any financial burden from the household
options.D: It completely cures the viral infection over time

explanation: Spot on! When loved ones offer emotional and everyday backing, it helps patients stay positive and stick to their medication schedules.

question: Why do large healthcare institutions maintain formal rules and standard operating procedures?

options.A: To replace the need for professional clinical judgment
options.B: To make sure employees never talk to upper management
options.C: To ensure consistent and fair patient care delivery
options.D: To slow down emergency responses on purpose

explanation: Formal rules create uniformity and fairness, ensuring that operations run predictably across departments. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the main reason body tissues get damaged once immune complexes settle in them?

options.A: Inflammation and enzyme release caused by white blood cells
options.B: Direct toxicity of the foreign serum on organ cells
options.C: Rapid multiplication of bacteria inside the trapped complexes
options.D: Complete blockage of oxygen supply to the major organs

explanation: Your white blood cells rush to help clear the mess, but their protective enzymes end up causing friendly fire on local tissues!

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse should do after an invasive ultrasound-guided procedure?

options.A: Check the patient's vital signs to make sure they are stable
options.B: Document the finished procedure in the patient chart
options.C: Give the family the final medical diagnosis
options.D: Watch the puncture site for bleeding or swelling

explanation: Nurses monitor recovery and report vital signs, but giving the final medical diagnosis is strictly the doctor's or radiologist's job.

question: Which hormone from the pituitary gland shoots up as the body approaches menopause?

options.A: Adrenocorticotropic hormone
options.B: Human growth hormone
options.C: Thyroid-stimulating hormone
options.D: Follicle-stimulating hormone

explanation: Think of the pituitary gland shouting louder (making more FSH) when the ovaries stop responding. Great revision point!

question: Which specific Nigerian law is dedicated to protecting the rights and welfare of children?

options.A: The Public Health Safety Code
options.B: The Child Rights Act
options.C: The National Minimum Wage Act
options.D: The Land Use Decree

explanation: Keep this one handy! The Child Rights Act is the key legal backing we use to protect Nigerian children against abuse, exploitation, and early marriage.

question: What is the primary purpose of using orthopedic traction?

options.A: To apply a pulling force to align bones and reduce spasms
options.B: To completely immobilize the patient without using any bed sheets
options.C: To permanently replace damaged joint cartilage without surgery
options.D: To deliver strong local pain medication directly into a fracture

question: What is the primary direction of time in a prospective research design?

options.A: Moving backward from the present into the past
options.B: Comparing two different time periods in history
options.C: Moving forward from the present into the future
options.D: Examining past medical records for current outcomes

explanation: Prospective studies are designed to follow participants forward in time to observe future outcomes. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h1)

question: What is the main reason for using the Z-track technique during an IM injection?

options.A: To numb the skin surface without using ice packs
options.B: To push blood vessels completely away from the needle tip
options.C: To prevent irritating medication from leaking into subcutaneous tissue
options.D: To make the needle go twice as deep into the bone

explanation: You've got it! Pulling the skin aside creates a zigzag track that traps the medicine deep inside the muscle, protecting the upper skin layers from irritation or stains.

question: Your patient stands on their tiptoes to grab a chart from a high shelf. What foot movement are they doing?

options.A: Dorsiflexion
options.B: Inversion
options.C: Plantar flexion
options.D: Supination

question: Why are patients with weak chest muscles at high risk for getting pneumonia?

options.A: Decreased room ventilation directly introduces bacteria into the lungs
options.B: Their immune systems completely stop producing white blood cells
options.C: Their body temperature constantly stays above normal limits
options.D: They cannot cough effectively to clear mucus from their airways

explanation: Coughing is our body's way of sweeping out trash. Without a strong cough, mucus stays stuck, and germs love to grow in it!

question: Why is it important for Nigerian student nurses to know local waste management laws?

options.A: To advocate for proper safety resources and ensure hospital compliance
options.B: To design new electrical furnaces for the hospital engineering team
options.C: To take over the daily responsibilities of the municipal sanitation department
options.D: To handle the legal prosecution of commercial waste contractors directly

explanation: When you know the rules, you can spot safety hazards, ask management for the right protective gear, and keep your patients and colleagues safe!

question: What is the primary physiological problem in clinical shock?

options.A: Inadequate blood flow and oxygen to tissues
options.B: An excessive buildup of red blood cells
options.C: A sudden drop in core body temperature
options.D: Severe localized pain in the chest

explanation: Shock happens when the circulatory system fails to deliver enough blood and oxygen to meet the basic needs of body tissues. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary focus of trait theories of personality?

options.A: Uncovering hidden sexual desires buried deep inside the human unconscious mind
options.B: Measuring stable, lifelong characteristics like extraversion and conscientiousness
options.C: Observing how physical rewards and punishments change everyday habits instantly
options.D: Tracking how childhood fever alters brain chemistry over many decades

explanation: Trait theories focus on identifying and measuring consistent behavior patterns or characteristics that remain relatively stable over time. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T8#GNS314_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which type of larvae is mainly responsible for causing myiasis (infestation of tissue) in humans?

options.A: Moth caterpillars
options.B: Dipterous fly larvae
options.C: Aquatic mosquito larvae
options.D: Seed tick arachnids

question: A family member worries that giving morphine will speed up their mother's death. What is your best response?

options.A: Agree to stop the medication immediately to respect the family's wishes
options.B: Tell them that morphine has no physical effect on terminal patients whatsoever
options.C: Suggest increasing the dose so the patient passes away more quickly and peacefully
options.D: Explain that correct doses relieve pain and distress without intentionally shortening life

explanation: It's a common worry! Reassure the family that proper pain relief is meant to ease suffering and dignity, not to hasten death.

question: What happens right after positive ions rush into a touch receptor during a physical push?

options.A: The receptor releases digestive enzymes
options.B: A local receptor potential forms
